name: Haiti
summary_text: Haiti is dangerous for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct is legal, but the state has effectively collapsed: gangs control most of Port-au-Prince, the police are outgunned, and mob violence against perceived LGBT people is documented. There is no LGR, no protection infrastructure, and no functioning judiciary. The trans-specific risk is inseparable from the generalised collapse — outing in gang-controlled territory can be lethal.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA World Database jurisdiction page for Haiti: documents the legal status of same-sex conduct and gender recognition.

sources.title: Human Dignity Trust
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Only the Human Dignity Trust homepage was retrievable at fetch time (no Haiti-specific page); Haiti does not criminalise same-sex conduct but has no protections and significant social hostility.

IGLHRC + SEROvie briefing paper: 'The Impact of the Earthquake, and Relief and Recovery Programs on Haitian LGBT People' - the 2010 earthquake heightened pre-existing inequalities; LGBT Haitians' particular vulnerabilities were largely ignored by officials and NGOs, with mistaken beliefs that LGBT people faced no greater risks or were undeserving of aid.

sources.title: Prominent Haitian LGBTQ activist found dead
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Nov 2019): a prominent Haitian LGBTQ activist was found dead - part of the pattern of violence against LGBT people in Haiti.
